text:
marta: quick heads-up — ran a perf job on 8xA100 with pp=4, tp=2, seq=2048 and saw a big PP bubble. throughput down ~18% vs baseline, wall time up, looks like all-reduce is stalling compute :/
kevin: ugh. any flamegraphs or nvprof traces?
yun: can you paste the profiler summary? curious about comm/compute overlap and microbatching config.
marta: paste from perf tool (trimmed):
```
Timeline summary: total_step=120
compute_time=520ms
all_reduce_total=270ms (34% of step)
idle_due_to_pp_bubble=180ms
microbatch_size=8
1F1B latency gap spikes at microbatch boundary
```
kevin: 34% AR overhead is high but not impossible. what's batch dim and kv cache behavior? are we sending full single-step grads or fused?
marta: using default grad-reduction (per-microbatch all-reduce) — not fused. KV cache warmup shows repeated small transfers, see logs: "kv_sync: sent 8 chunks, avg 3KB"
yun: small frequent transfers + unfused all-reduce = lots of small comm ops. with tp=2 you're also touching cross-node slice boundaries — increases latency. Try increasing microbatch_size or enable chunked fused all-reduce.
kevin: also check 1F1B schedule params; if microbatch count <= pp_depth we get bubble. what's microbatch count?
marta: microbatch_count=8, pp_depth=4 -> microbatches per stage = 2, 1F1B schedule still leaves gaps when AR latency spikes.
sam: quick idea — try microbatch_count=16 (microbatch_size halves) so 1F1B keeps pipeline fed longer and ARs amortize? or enable async all-reduce (overlap with next microbatch compute).
yun: agreed. two concrete experiments: (A) microbatch_count=16, enable fused_allreduce=true, (B) keep microbatch_count=8 but enable NCCL async progress + allreduce fusion. measure step_time and comm_percent.
marta: running A now on ci-perf-08, will post numbers. ETA ~10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
perf-bot: Job 2026-04-02_09:12:32 started: 8xA100 pp=4 tp=2 seq=2048 mbatches=16 fused_allreduce=true
marta: results (A): step_time median 65ms -> baseline 80ms, throughput +22%, all_reduce_total down to 120ms (from 270ms), bubble idle ~40ms
kevin: nice improvement. that suggests fusion & more microbatches helps amortize AR.
yun: can we quantify comm/compute overlap? any traces showing concurrent streams?
marta: nvprof snippet shows overlap ~45ms overlapped out of 120ms AR, so about 37% overlapped. not perfect but better.
sam: what's KV cache pattern after change? did smaller microbatch size increase KV syncs?
marta: KV syncs increased in count but each sync is smaller; total KV bytes ~same. latency per KV chunk lower due to batching inside transport.
kevin: follow-up: try enabling 1F1B tuning parameters: pipeline_idle_target=0.05, enable_comm_prepost=true — prepost posts pending ARs slightly earlier. should reduce bubble further.
marta: kick off B now with async NCCL and prepost flags.
perf-bot: Job 2026-04-02_09:33:10 started: config: async_nccl=true prepost_comm=true microbatch_count=8 fused_allreduce=true
marta: results (B): step_time median 62ms, all_reduce_total 110ms, overlapped 60ms, bubble ~20ms. throughput +26% vs baseline.
yun: good win. sounds like three levers: increase microbatching, fuse/reduce small ARs, and prepost/async to overlap comm earlier.
kevin: note tradeoffs — larger microbatches may increase latency tail for single requests and increase memory pressure (KV cache). need SLO-aware defaults.
marta: agreed. i'll draft a runtime PR to:
- enable fused_allreduce by default on pp>=2 when microbatch_count>8
- add auto_tune: try microbatch_count x2 when comm overhead >25%
- expose prepost_comm flag and enable in CI perf profiles
I'll add perf numbers and flamegraphs to PR.
sam: also add a regression test that runs 8xA100 seq=2048 nightly to catch regressions.
yun: and instrument kernel selection heuristics to prefer larger-fused-kernel variants when comm is hotspot.
marta: SGTM. thanks team — will open PR and link perf artifacts. :rocket:
